note_tweet.text: Not the same. Dots is currently one primary always-on agent with its own cloud computer, shared context across ChatGPT/Slack/Teams, and customizable approval rules for actions. It can run parallel background tasks and hand off to Work/Codex, but it lacks Grok Bot’s multi-named-bot model where agents share context freely and hand work off with less mandatory approvals. The day-to-day friction is closer to a single tunable agent than Grok’s parallel roster.

note_tweet.text:
Muse Email is useful. Test one: Email it Kindle highlights from a Spanish book for it to add to my Spanish Vocab app. Test two: Have my work ChatGPT Dot email it things to do, like adding work travel to my family calendar.

You have to verify email addresses that your Muse can act on, which I had to do for my work email. Once you do, it can just do stuff that you ask by email, and also reply to those emails.

It executes the work silently in the background, then lets you know what it's done when it's complete. There seems to be a background agent that handles the incoming email tasks, then notifies the main agent when something's done and it needs to alert the user.

Overall, like everything with Muse, this is very well-executed and user-friendly. The two issues I've noticed so far: (1) an email verification weirdly expiring right after I verified it and (2) clicking the ⚙️ icon for the email tool on desktop opening the Connectors index pane rather than opening the email connector setting pane.
